full_judgment: 5. It is vehemently argued on behalf of the petitioner that the local Upazila Administration headed by the respondent No.6, UNO, in conspiracy and collaboration with the Upazila Development Co-ordination Committee and the local politically influential persons aided by their mastans, try to control the lease of the Cattle Hat in question and other Hat Bazars in the area. As a part of this man oeuvre and conspiracy in retaining the control over the said Cattle Hat, the aforesaid syndicate tried to ensure that the said Cattle Hat was not taken on lease in auction by any genuine auction purchasers and traders of the area on a free fair public auction. In most times, this syndicate headed by the UNO make a show of holding public auction for lease of the said cattle Hat and other Hat Bazars in the locality and retain control over them either keeping them under khas collection on the plea that no bidder turned up or that the bid was not satisfactory or by obtaining the lease on its price by preventing others from participating in the tender by resorting to positive act of coercion and intimidation. In this way, this syndicate kept the said Cattle Hat under khas collection for quite some time and misappropriated bulk of the money collected on khas collection showing lesser amount than the amount was actually collected on the plea that no bidders turned up when the said Cattle Hat was put up on auction on 3(three) consecutive dates. When the auction for the said Cattle Hat was advertised for the 4th time the petitioner came to know of the same and wanted to participate in the auction but he was not allowed by the syndicate to buy the tender documents to participate in the auction fixed on 13-4-2005, so that the syndicate could get the lease of the said cattle Hat on their price. The petitioner, it is further submitted, having come to know that the said Cattle Hat would be put on auction for lease on 13-4-2005 he wanted to participate in the auction to make a bid for taking lease of the said Hat at Taka 22,00,000 (taka twenty-two lac). Accordingly, he made a deposit of Taka 4,50,000 by two Bank Drafts dated 29-3-2005 with a local branch of Sonali Bank in the name of UNO as Call Deposit by way of earnest money at the rate of 20% of his total intended bid money as per Clause (3) of the Guide Lines regarding Management and Lease of the Government Hat Bazars dated 20-7-2002 issued by the Ministry of Local Government and Rural Development vide Memo. No প্রজেই-২/২-৫/২০০০/৪০৮(৫২৭২). But because of the act of intimidation and coercion of the said syndicate the petitioner could not buy the tender documents and participate in the auction held on 13-4-2005. The syndicate however, submitted 6(six) bids in six different names of its members to the exclusion of the petitioner and the bid of the respondent No. 7, being one of the members of the syndicate was shown to have been the highest for Taka 20,01,000 (taka twenty lac one thousand) and it was accepted for granting lease of the said Cattle Hat in favour of respondent No.7. The petitioner accordingly, made representations dated 16-4-2005 and 26-4-2005 to the respondent No.4, Deputy Commissioner, to grant lease of the said Cattle Hat to him at Taka 22,00,000 (Taka twenty-two lac) as this was higher than the amount quoted by the respondent No.7. But the respondent Nos. 4 and 6 without paying any heed to the petitioner's representations decided to grant lease of the said Cattle Hat to the respondent No.7 and thus committed an illegality, it is argued.
